issues.claim: R4-13 made the disaster's unit count two-stage. §10.2 (c) (l. 15631–15635) keeps round(s × n) clamped to [1, n] as every place's count, and then "the `neighbourhoods` place … draws at least every matched target (max(k, |`matched`|)) and, by fire, stops where its order ends, the shortfall reported (V01 §3.16 (5))". V01 §3.16 (5) (l. 2361–2366), the home, takes "the first max(k, |`matched`|) units of the order — all of a shorter fire order". V12 l. 2709 agrees. V07 §5.6 (1) (l. 3411–3415) still equates the look's units with the first stage: "A look scaled as a share of its place's units (§10.2 (c)) takes … round(s × n) clamped to [1, n] where s is above 0 and none where it is not — V01 §3.16 (5)'s count of the disaster's units, read for every share at the village rungs". T-V7-69 (c) bars the same ("a look scaled as a share of its place's n units at share s takes round(s × n) clamped to [1, n] where s is above 0"). Take a VILLAGE of four ends and a calamity naming two of them at severity 0: s = 0.05, so k = round(0.2) clamped to 1. V07 strikes one end, V01 strikes both, and a correct build fails T-V7-69 (c). A fire whose order ends before k gives a third outcome. R4-13's routing named only pipeline and V12. Two units, two outcomes for one case (R3-03 (b)).
issues.required_change: V07 §5.6 (1): after "… round(s × n) clamped to [1, n] where s is above 0 and none where it is not" replace "— V01 §3.16 (5)'s count of the disaster's units, read for every share at the village rungs," with "— §10.2 (c)'s count k, read for every share at the village rungs," and, after "… never rounds to nothing", add: "; the disaster's `neighbourhoods` place then strikes at least every matched target — the first max(k, |`matched`|) units of its order — and, by fire, stops where its order ends, the shortfall reported (V01 §3.16 (5), the home)". T-V7-69 (c): after "… takes round(s × n) clamped to [1, n] where s is above 0" add "— a disaster's units the first max(k, |`matched`|) of its order, k that count, or all of a shorter fire order (V01 §3.16 (5)) — on a VILLAGE fixture whose calamity names more ends than k (every named end struck) and on a fire whose order ends before k (the shortfall reported)".

issues.claim: R4-12: "Every Find reader at a drawn week reads that listing over the model the view draws". §11.2 *At a drawn week* (l. 16455–16463) makes the listing the frame's ("every row, count, match and gap unit") wherever that week's frame is not the head. V01 §5.4, the town's reading, now reads the frame (lead l. 3139–3142; (1) l. 3167–3171; (3) l. 3188–3191; (4) a change of the drawn week re-evaluates). V01 §5.4's lead hands the village rungs to V07 §5.5 ("Below TOWN the village's reading is V07 §5.5's"), and V09 §4.21.10 (3) and (10) read V07 §5.5 there. V07 §5.5 (1) (l. 3339) builds the list "by §11.2's gazetteer query over the committed records", and W83 (l. 291) says the same. (2)'s gap units are the ends with no date. (4) re-evaluates on "Every commit, regenerate, undo, village epoch and hand-off" but not on a change of the drawn week. T-V7-68 runs no scrubbed week. So at a scrubbed VILLAGE week whose frame is not the head, one builder lists, glows and gaps the head's ends and uses (V07), and another the frame's (§11.2, V01). Examples are a smithy an epoch opened after that week, or two ends merged since. This is the class R4-12 graded major (VRC3T-01, VV12-r3-03, VAL-R3-05); R4-12's sweep did not reach V07.
issues.required_change: V07 §5.5 (1): "built by §11.2's gazetteer query over the committed records" → "built by §11.2's gazetteer query over the model the view draws — the committed head or, at a drawn week (§2.9's `week`) whose frame is not the head, V06 §3.15.2's frame (§11.2's *At a drawn week*) —"; its **areas** bullet adds "at such a week, the ends and field groups that frame holds". (2) adds: "At a drawn week whose frame is not the head, the units and their members are read over that frame (§11.2's *At a drawn week*; V01 §5.4 (3)): an end the frame lacks is no unit." (4): "Every commit, regenerate, undo, village epoch and hand-off re-evaluates the chips at once" → "Every commit, regenerate, undo, village epoch and hand-off, and every change of the view's drawn week (§2.9's `week`), re-evaluates the chips at once". W83's input cell "§11.2's gazetteer at the view's effective key over the committed records" → "§11.2's gazetteer at the view's effective key and drawn week (§11.2's *At a drawn week*; V06 §3.15.2's frame)". T-V7-68 adds: "at a scrubbed week whose frame is not the head, on a VILLAGE fixture whose later epoch opened a smithy, closed another's use and merged two ends, each chip's matches, the ends listed and Show gaps' units equal §11.2's listing at that week, and the head's are back at the head". Its timing cell adds "its scrubbed-week clause at the first exit after M6-E's history frames (V06 §8, E6)".

issues.claim: R4-03 made an element a restoring event's re-cut mints enter the damage only when that restoration ends: "Before that week it is drawn as built" (V06 §3.23 (3)). V03 §5.6 (2) (a) (l. 2693–2694: "an element is compared with the level only from its entry week") and §2.6 step 7 (l. 2099–2101) carry it. R4-03's sweep cleared §8.6 and V02 l. 3058 for the `decayPeak` they read. Their restatements of the *damaged* comparison still omit the entry week. §8.6's lead (l. 14069–14072) has "each plan element whose threshold t … its decay level reaches at the drawn week (… damaged while the level is above 0 and at least t — §6.3 *Plan damage*'s one comparison every reader makes) is drawn damaged". V02 §5.7 (2) (l. 3057–3063) has "damaged, by §6.3 *Plan damage*'s one comparison (the level above 0 and at least its keyed threshold t …)", and it names only "a wing an `extend` adds, an element a re-cut makes … added after its building's damage left" as drawn as built. During a `reoccupy` whose `repair` Works still runs, a minted room's roof bay or partition whose t the level reaches is damaged by these two texts and as built by V03, V06 and §2.6. Both texts take each element's state from V03's `planDamage` (V03 §5.6 (3); V02 §5.7 (2): "V03's damage layer gives each element its state"), so nothing built changes. This is VDC4-01's case (§6.3, the home) at two restatements.
issues.required_change: One fix with VDC4-01. §8.6's lead: after "(V06's `decayLevel`; damaged while the level is above 0 and at least t" insert ", compared from the element's entry week into the plan (V03 §5.6 (2) (a)–(b); an element a restoring event's re-cut mints from the week that restoration ends, before which it draws as built, V06 §3.23 (3))". END at V02 §5.7 (2): "damaged, by §6.3 *Plan damage*'s one comparison (the level above 0 and at least its keyed threshold t: §6.3's `plan.damage`, V11's ranges)" adds "from the element's entry week into the plan (V03 §5.6 (2) (a))", and "so an element added after its building's damage left (a wing an `extend` adds, an element a re-cut makes) is drawn as built" → "so an element added after its building's damage left (a wing an `extend` adds, an element a re-cut makes), or one a restoring event's re-cut mints (V06 §3.23 (3)), is drawn as built".

issues.claim: repair-r4-V03's HAND-OFF 1 (round 5's verifiers): §16's M3b row (l. 20181) lands "the `disaster` look's districts (§10.2's `neighbourhoods`) with volume 1's `disasterSource` and `disasterDistricts` at M5 (W10)". At THORP, HAMLET and VILLAGE the look's units are V07 §5.6 (3)'s and land at V-M3. V03 §8 (l. 2959–2960, P4's exit), T-V3-40's timing cell, J-V3.140, V02 §8.6 (l. 3893–3894), T-V1-60 and T-V7-69 all say so, as does §10.2's lead ("at the village rungs before V07's step the village draws no disaster unit"). The base's build-plan row names neither the village units nor their milestone, and it writes "districts" where R4-04 (a)'s phrase is "the look's units". §10.2's lead states the landing, so nothing built changes.
issues.required_change: §16's M3b row: "the `disaster` look's districts (§10.2's `neighbourhoods`) with volume 1's `disasterSource` and `disasterDistricts` at M5 (W10)" → "the `disaster` look's units (§10.2's `neighbourhoods`) with volume 1's `disasterSource` and `disasterDistricts` at M5 (W10) — at the village rungs volume 7's `villageDisasterUnits` and `villageUnitPlots`, V-M3 (V07 §5.6 (8)) —", the rest as it stands.
